text: Respirology consult. Impression: moderate asthma. Former smoker, 10 pack-years.
Assessment: possible asthma vs COPD. Eosinophils were 0.5 x 10^9/L last year.
Mepolizumab 100 mg SC every 4 weeks was started on February 3, 2025.
Respirology review. Diagnosis: severe asthma with an eosinophilic phenotype, confirmed on repeat spirometry. Dupilumab was discussed but the patient declined.
Mepolizumab discontinued on 2025-08-20 because of injection-site reactions and no improvement in exacerbations.
Asthma flare-up. Prednisone 50 mg daily x 5 days.
Seen for acute asthma attack. Given dexamethasone 16 mg orally in the department, then prednisolone 50 mg daily for 4 more days.
Follow-up after ED visit. Completed prednisolone course from the ED. Asthma improving. DOB on old referral listed as 1957-07-02 in error.

Medication review.
Medications:
Budesonide/formoterol 200/6 mcg 2 puffs twice daily
Montelukast 10 mg daily
Terbutaline 0.5 mg as needed (discontinued)
Contact dermatitis on both forearms. Hydrocortisone 1% cream twice daily for 7 days.
Asthma flare-up triggered by wildfire smoke. Prednisone 50 mg daily x 5 days prescribed.
Patient smokes 5 cigarettes a day again since March. Partner also smokes.
Hematology. Specimen collected: July 14, 2026. Absolute eosinophils: 380 cells/uL. Sputum eosinophils 3%.
Mild wheeze. Patient asked whether to start prednisone; advised to use reliever first. No steroids given.
Stepped up from Symbicort 200/6 to Trelegy Ellipta 100/62.5/25 mcg one inhalation daily.
